title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is smooth, proper and geometrically connected of dimension n over F_p (p stands for the cardinality of the base field). E is a smooth ℓ-adic sheaf, and f is the Frobenius acting on H^i(X̄, Ē). E is assumed self-dual up to a Tate twist: Ě ≅ E(ρ). The 'dual' sheaf DE therefore has the same cohomology as E up to a twist, so L_{DE}(t) = L_E(p^{-(n+ρ)} t).

The previous step (2) is presumably the Poincaré-duality form of the functional equation, relating L_E at 1/t to L_{DE}. The pairing H^i(X̄,Ē) × H^{2n-i}(X̄,Ě) → H^{2n}(X̄,Q_ℓ) = Q_ℓ(-n) is perfect. Substituting and replacing t by t^{-1} gives
(3) L_E(1/(p^{n+ρ} t)) = ε(E) (-p^{(n+ρ)/2} t)^{χ(E)} L_E(t),
where ε(E) is the sign of det(f | H^*) in the alternating sense, i.e. ∏ (sign det f|H^i)^{(-1)^i}.

Normalising ξ_E(t) = t^{χ/2} L_E(t) gives the symmetric functional equation
ξ(1/(p^{n+ρ} t)) = ε'(E) ξ(t), with ε' = (-1)^χ ε = ±1.

Grothendieck then simplifies the sign:
- Duality identifies H^{2n-i}(Ē) with the dual of H^i(Ē), twisted by a power of Q_ℓ(1).
- Frobenius acts on Q_ℓ(1) by a positive scalar.
- Hence det f on H^{2n-i} has the same sign as det f on H^i, i.e. ε_i = ε_{2n-i}.
- So all factors except the middle one cancel in pairs: ε(E) = sign det(f | H^n).
- Likewise b_i = b_{2n-i} gives χ ≡ b_n mod 2.
- Hence ε'(E) = (-1)^{b_n(E)} sign det(f | H^n(X̄,Ē)).

Purpose: to state the functional equation of the cohomological L-function of a self-dual sheaf in 'completed' symmetric form, and to identify the root number as a middle-cohomology invariant. This is a step toward the Bourbaki exposé 279 / SGA 5 treatment of rationality and the functional equation. The paper is the back of a 1962 La Tribu typescript, so this is early (ca. 1962–64).
errors: No substantive error. Writing u = p^{n+ρ}t, one checks ξ(1/u) = (p^{n+ρ}t)^{-χ/2} ε (-1)^χ p^{(n+ρ)χ/2} t^χ L(t) = (-1)^χ ε ξ(t), confirming ε' = (-1)^χ ε.
The parity step (-1)^χ = (-1)^{b_n} needs b_i = b_{2n-i}, which follows from Ě ≅ E(ρ) together with Poincaré duality. This holds under the stated self-duality.
Notational slips: the first sign formula writes F̄ for Ē, and the last line drops the bars (H^n(X,E) should be H^n(X̄,Ē)).
'ε(E) = signe det' is a slight abuse: det f|H^* equals ±p^{(n+ρ)χ/2}, and ε(E) is the sign of that quantity. This is implicit in the text.

ideas.what: Functional equation of L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves on proper smooth varieties via Poincaré duality, with L_{DE}(t) = L_E(p^{-(n+ρ)}t) for self-dual-up-to-twist E
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck functional equation for cohomological L-functions
ideas.where_published: Sém. Bourbaki exp. 279 'Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L' (1964); SGA 5

ideas.what: Completed function ξ_E(t) = t^{χ/2} L_E(t) satisfying ξ(1/(q^w t)) = ±ξ(t)
ideas.modern_name: symmetric/completed form of the zeta functional equation

ideas.what: Sign of the functional equation equals (-1)^{b_n} times the sign of det Frobenius on middle cohomology, via cancellation ε_i = ε_{2n-i}
ideas.modern_name: global root number as determinant of Frobenius on middle cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Grothendieck/Deligne; later Saito's work on the sign of the functional equation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine draft computation of the sign in the functional equation for self-dual ℓ-adic sheaves. The reduction to det of Frobenius on H^n is well known and appears in standard treatments; it is of interest only as an early (ca. 1962–64) dated draft.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'portant dans (2) [?]' – the handwriting is hard to read; it may be 'portant dans ces[?]', but in any case it refers to the preceding duality formula.
In the first sign formula, 'H^i(X̄, F̄)' and 'H^*(X̄, F̄)' should be read as H^i(X̄, Ē) and H^*(X̄, Ē).
The 'valeurs dans Q_ℓ(1)… Q_ℓ(n)' passage concerns the duality pairing taking values in a Tate twist Q_ℓ(−n)/(ρ), together with the observation that Frobenius acts on Q_ℓ(1) by a positive scalar.
